results.summary: The Aero Hand tab now centers on teaching: a big Record button, a Recordings list with Play, Rename and Delete, and every other command in one Commands menu.
results.detailed_description:
The left half of the tab is now one big red Record button. While it records you see a red dot, a running timer, a live bar for each of the seven servos (0% open to 100%) and a big Stop button. Stop saves the recording.

The right half lists your recordings, newest first, with the name (or the date if it has none) and the length. Each one has Play, a pencil to rename it and a trash can to delete it. Delete moves the file into takes/deleted rather than erasing it, so a wrong click can be undone. Play uses the speed dropdown like everything else.

Everything else is in one Commands dropdown at the top: the poses (including thumbs up and relax), Test, Dance, Count to ten, Teleop, Re-home, and Rock paper scissors. Speed and Hold sit right next to it, with the small log button and Stop. The log is still hidden by default, and the window still fills the screen and can go full screen.

What I tested on the real hand: a 3-second recording ran at 100 Hz and streamed the live positions. Nobody was here to move the fingers, so I played a made-up recording instead (index and middle curl, then half open), and the hand ended within about 1° of where the recording said. The app builds, but I didn't open it. Your test is still needed: press Record, move a finger, press Stop, then Play it.

results.identified_issue: A macOS target (HelpingHandsMac) already existed, so no new target was needed. AeroHandRunner (Mac only) runs third_party/aero_hand/scripts/*.sh through /bin/sh via Process. TCC assigns child processes to the responsible app, which is why the permissions belong to Helping Hands: added NSCameraUsageDescription and NSAppleEventsUsageDescription, plus an entitlements file (camera, audio-input, apple-events, no sandbox) so a future hardened or notarized build keeps working. Stop sends SIGINT first so the scripts' finally blocks ease the hand open, then SIGTERM after 3 s. A new command interrupts the running one and starts after it exits, because there's only one serial port. URLs are caught by a kAEGetURL Apple Event handler in AeroURLDelegate, because onOpenURL on the Mac opens a new window for each URL. Verified: the scratch xcodegen build compiles. open -a <scratch app> 'helpinghands://aero/pose/rock on' and 'teleop/dry-run' reached a stub script, including a cold launch, and fast/on set AERO_SPEED_PCT=100. A screenshot shows the panel loading all of the poses. Not verified: real hardware runs from the app, the camera prompt, and the LaunchServices claim of the scheme from /Applications (the scratch build in /tmp wasn't eligible). Teleop's preview is still the cv2.imshow window. Embedding it in the app would need the app to own the capture and pipe frames to Python. The iOS target shares the bundle id but doesn't register the scheme.
